Blocks.Text: Attending Physician: Dr. Michael Robert Jackson, MD
Page injection(s) | DOB: 04/25/1958 I MRN: MRN 12233 | Date: 01/20/2024
Place of Service: On Campus-Outpatient Hospital (Code 22)
Procedure Location: Atlanta Heart & Vascular Center
Chest pain and shortness of breath on exertion, worsening over 3 months.
Mr. Thompson reports increasing chest pain with exertion over the past 3 months. Pain is
substernal, pressure-like, radiates to left arm. Associated with dyspnea and diaphoresis.
Symptoms occur with minimal exertion (1 block). No rest pain. Patient describes classic
anginal symptoms with progressive worsening, now limiting his daily activities.
Diabetes mellitus type 2 - managed with metformin
Family history of coronary artery disease (father had MI at age 58)
No previous cardiac procedures or hospitalizations
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs, gallops, or rubs. Point of maximal
Pulmonary: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no rales or wheezes
Extremities: No edema, peripheral pulses intact
Page 1 of 1 Patient: William Thompson | DOB: 04/25/1958 I MRN: MRN112233 | Date: 01/20/2024
T wave flattening in leads V4-V6
Regional wall motion abnormalities in LAD territory
Positive for ischemia at 75% maximum heart rate
Exercise capacity limited by chest pain and dyspnea
I25.10 - Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
Mr. Thompson has stable angina with high pre-test probability of significant coronary
artery disease. Stress test is positive for ischemia in LAD distribution. Echocardiogram
shows regional wall motion abnormalities consistent with coronary artery disease. Given
the high-risk findings and progressive symptoms, cardiac catheterization is indicated for
1. Stable angina with high-risk stress test - Patient has classic anginal symptoms with
2. Positive stress test with significant ST depression >2mm - Indicates high-grade
3. Regional wall motion abnormalities on echocardiogram - Consistent with prior
4. Symptoms limiting daily activities - Progressive functional limitation
5. High pre-test probability of CAD - Based on age, gender, and multiple risk factors
6. Failed optimal medical therapy - Symptoms persist despite appropriate medications
7. Need for risk stratification - To determine appropriate treatment strategy
Page 1 of 1 Patient: William Thompson DOB: 04/25/1958 I MRN: MRN112233 | Date: 01/20/2024
Procedure: Diagnostic cardiac catheterization with coronary angiography and left heart
Approach: Right radial artery access (preferred) or right femoral artery
Selective coronary angiography of left and right coronary systems
Left ventriculography to assess wall motion and ejection fraction
Potential for ad hoc percutaneous coronary intervention if appropriate
Location: Atlanta Heart & Vascular Center Cardiac Catheterization Laboratory
Cardiac catheterization is medically necessary for Mr. Thompson due to his high-risk
presentation with stable angina, positive stress test with significant ST changes, and
regional wall motion abnormalities on echocardiogram. The procedure is indicated per
ACC/AHA guidelines for patients with high-risk non-invasive testing results. Without
definitive coronary anatomy assessment, the patient remains at risk for major adverse
cardiac events including myocardial infarction and sudden cardiac death.
Patient has been counseled on the risks and benefits of cardiac catheterization including
but not limited to: bleeding, infection, contrast nephropathy, stroke, myocardial infarction,
and death (risk <0.1%). Benefits include definitive diagnosis of coronary anatomy, risk
stratification, and potential for therapeutic intervention. Patient understands and agrees to
